posts.caption:
They say it’s what’s inside that counts, and that’s certainly the case for these #Chanel Fall 2026 #HauteCouture jackets. What looked like deceptively simple tweed jackets on the runway tells a completely different story once opened, revealing silk linings covered in illustrations depicting the very fairy tales that inspired #MatthieuBlazy’s collection. Hidden inside are scenes from Jack and the Beanstalk, Goldilocks, and Puss in Boots.
A jacket lining, which traditionally functions to conceal construction and provide comfort, is turned into a private work of art reserved only for the wearer. It’s such a beautiful continuation of the collection’s theme of hidden narratives, where some of the details aren’t immediately visible from the outside.

posts.caption:
#Chloé may have just released the most beautiful campaign of Fall 2026 so far. Starring #RaquelZimmermann and photographed by legendary duo @inezandvinoodh, it’s a folkloric fantasy that perfectly captures #ChemenaKamali’s romantic vision for the French house.
I remember seeing the collection debut, it was a #KateBush in the ‘70s meets handmade clothes passed down from mother to daughter. Chloé’s bohemian heritage came to life through ruffles, delicate lace, sheer silks, Victorian-inspired blouses, folkloric dresses and sweeping capes, creating a wardrobe that felt both nostalgic and romantic.

posts.caption:
#Gabbriette’s gothic @matieresfecales wedding wardrobe was one of the most beautiful I’ve seen this year and a welcome change from the minimalist gowns that have dominated bridal trends.
The ceremony gown, titled “Gabriella,” was a mutated and distressed Victorian-inspired silk taffeta dress reminiscent of Winona Ryder’s red dress in Bram Stoker’s #Dracula (1992), complete with a four layer bustle.
For the rehearsal dinner, an old Maison Margiela dress of the brides was modified by adding layers of hand-cut, distressed tulle. The third look was a tailored leather suit paired with a satin top hat by #StephenJones. Each look completed with a custom pair of #ChristianLouboutin x #MatièresFécales curved heels.

posts.caption:
India's Renee Noronha has won first place in the 18-24 category at the Ironman Philippines. Completing the gruelling challenge at 15:55:37, the 20-year-old IIT Madras student upheld held her record of being the youngest Indian female Ironman finisher.
Renee battled torrential rains and unforgiving temperatures to complete the race. In conversation with SheThePeople, the triathlete also revealed that she participated on day 3 of her period, making the victory a profound reminder of her strength and resilience as a woman.
With this win, Renee has now qualified for the Ironman World Championship Hawaii, scheduled for October 2026. She is also on a mission to set a new Guinness world record to become the youngest person in the world to do a full Ironman on 6 continents. She is on track to achieve this by April 2027, at the age of 21.
Read full interview at www.shethepeople.tv. | @renee.noronha

posts.caption:
I cannot just keep people around me for fun and use them to heal my boredom! As someone who considers herself a deep thinker, empathetic and honest, I value the friendships I have lost in my life.
They have always been the ones I have held close to my heart and an integral part of my life. Friendships are so transient throughout our entire life; in our initial days, we fathom the number of our friendships with the number of people who were there in our lives or the number of friendship bands someone tied to our hands.
Remember being the cool kid when you were in your third standard, and your hands were filled to the brim with no more place to tie a friendship band- how much would we reek of awesomeness back then. It was amusing and refreshing how friendships would feel so easy and reassuring; our games would be the centre of our world.

posts.caption:
What happens when an artist’s heart flutters like a butterfly between two skills? To gain the response to this question, we have to observe Prachi Saathi’s life closely.
When she was a child, her mother enrolled her at the Prithvi summer camp, where she began to learn voice-dubbing, a skill she picked up without purpose. Later, she got an opportunity to work as a voice-dubbing actor in a children’s film, Karamati Coat, which gained her recognition in the field.
Today, she is a renowned voice-dubbing actress. Prachi, who has been the official Hindi dubbing voice for Disney character Minnie Mouse, has voice-dubbed over 200 character roles in foreign animation media in the Indian dubbing industry. She is also a Bharatanatyam dancer and is currently training under her Guru, Smt. Rama Vaidyanathan.
Visit www.shethepeople.tv to read the full interview by @_shivanilamba

It is a profession that takes years to build. The eye. The contacts. The knowledge of how the industry actually works across every sector, every brief, every type of client. That does not come from loving fashion. It comes from years of showing up, doing the work and figuring it out mostly alone.
And yet it is still one of the most undervalued roles in the creative industry.
Stylists are asked to work for free. For credit. For exposure. For a rate that does not come close to reflecting the skill, the hours or the experience involved. And somewhere along the way the industry decided that was normal. That stylists should be grateful for the opportunity. That loving what you do means you should not expect to be paid properly for it.
We are past that.
Behind every iconic image, every red carpet moment, every campaign that stopped you mid-scroll, there was a stylist. Building the looks, interpreting the brief, managing the pressure, absorbing the chaos so nobody else had to. Often without a credit. Sometimes without a proper rate.
That changes when stylists know their worth, charge it without apology and stop accepting the jobs that treat their career like a favour.
➡️➡️ If you are a working fashion stylist who is ready to do exactly that, comment STUDIO and we will send you the free trial link to The Studio of Stylist Elixir. Rate guides. Contracts. Portfolio tools. Masterclasses every Monday. Everything you need to build a career that reflects what you are actually worth.

Jonathan Anderson just showed his first couture collection for Dior. If you do not understand why it mattered, this post is for you.

John Galliano was front row. The artisans were the opening act. The silhouettes came from ceramicist Magdalene Odundo.

If you are in Paris: the show space at Musée Rodin opens to the public from 28 January for one week. The new couture collection, archival Dior pieces, and the Odundo ceramics that inspired it. You can see it yourself.

This is not about liking or not liking a collection. This is about understanding what you are looking at.
The Studio of Stylist Elixir is our online membership. Guides. Templates. Live calls. A community of stylists who are learning and building together. Comment ‘studio’ for a free trial.

Doors close this Friday, 31st July, just two days away. And this is the last Fashion Mentorship I am running in 2026.
Six weeks to stop winging your styling career and start building it properly, with me beside you the whole way.
It’s for fashion creatives at every level. Whether you are just starting out and unsure of your next step, or you have been assisting for a while and want to make the leap to lead stylist, or you are booking work but it has gone quiet and inconsistent, this is for you.
Over the six weeks, together we work on:
➡️Why you are not booking the clients you want, and how to change it
➡️Why your repeat bookings dried up, and how to bring them back
➡️Why your pitches get compliments but never bookings
➡️Pricing your worth without the fear
➡️Building a portfolio that actually books you
➡️Growing from scratch, or pivoting from assisting into lead stylist
But honestly, some of the most important work I do with my mentees isn’t in the masterclasses at all. It is the messy, real-life stuff. The boundary you are scared to set. The quiet month that makes you panic. The invoice or the client situation you do not know how to handle. That is the part no one teaches you, and it is exactly where I want to be beside you. I have been in every one of these situations myself.
You can join as part of the group, or privately 1:1 with me if you would rather stay anonymous because of the clients you work with.
It all happens inside The Studio, with 1:1 support from me throughout, so you are never doing it alone.
This is the last time I am running this in 2026, and doors close this Friday, 31st July. If you are reading this and thinking, Emily, this is me, I want in, then DM me the word MENTORSHIP or tap the link in my bio. I would love to have you. x

posts.caption:
Imagine your career is a bath you are trying to fill. All the effort you pour in, the posting, the pitching, the networking, the portfolio, all of it, that is the tap, the water running in.
Now imagine there are holes around the bath. You are filling it a little, but nothing stays. You can turn that tap on as hard as you like, but if the bath is full of holes, it will never fill.
A business that is losing the clients, that is slowly emptying, does not need to work harder and faster. It needs the leaks named, and then it needs you to fix them.
Here is what changes when you find them, and plug them one by one. A stranger can find you, understand you, trust you, and book you, without ever having met you at a party or been sent by a friend of a friend. And that is the difference between a career that runs on luck and a small circle, and a career that you actually control.
It is the reason my 6-Week Fashion Mentorship Program exists. The Fashion Mentorship Program is not for stylists further ahead than you. It is for stylists like you. The stylists brave enough to take a leap and look inwards at their business are the ones who win. If you have felt these leaks as you read, that is your sign this is for you.
The Fashion Mentorship Program starts on Saturday, and the last chance to enrol is on Friday 31st. I would love this to be the season that finally changes for you.
DM mentor of follow the link in the bio 💚

Sheet masks were never designed to be beauty’s side character. Yet for years, their brief rarely moved beyond a quick hit of hydration.

The format has since caught up with increasingly ambitious skincare routines. Taking cues from Korean beauty, newer masks combine longer wear times with more targeted ingredients, promising bounce, brightness, barrier support and hydration in a single sheet.

Nykaa Collection’s (@nykaacollection) Skin’s collagen masks bring vegan PDRN and vitamin C into the mix. The hydrogel sheets gradually turn transparent as they sit on the skin, making them better suited to longer wear, including overnight use.

The proposition is less about replacing an entire routine than making the sheet mask work harder within one: before a meeting, after a long day or while sleeping.

Arooj Aftab (@aroojaftab) became a symbol before many people had even heard the music. Her 2022 Grammy win for ‘Mohabbat’ made international success feel newly possible for South Asian artistes, especially women raised to believe that certain stages were simply not built with them in mind.

The milestone made Aftab a cultural shorthand for unimaginable success, as she kept moving between jazz, ghazals, Urdu poetry, and electronic riffs, refusing to turn identity into a neat creative instruction.

She understands what being first can unlock: doors that appear less firmly shut and ambitions that no longer feel faintly delusional.

Aftab’s music carries where she comes from without presenting it for inspection. Her achievement widened the scope of South Asian ambition; her career insists that representation should never become its ceiling.

Read the full interview at the link in bio.
By Arshia Dhar (@urseaa)

posts.caption:
Radio was the original parasocial relationship: a familiar voice in traffic, after break-ups, through power cuts, and before Google Maps knew the route.
For two decades, private FM gave Indian cities their own jokes, moods, and minor celebrities, all without a feed. Now stations are surrendering licences, Gen Z is on Spotify, and the algorithm has inherited the aux.
What disappears with radio is more than music. It is the strange intimacy of thousands of people hearing the same voice, at the same time, in the same city.
Full story at the link in bio.
By Karishma Kuenzang (@kkuenzang)
#radio #spotify

Mirabai Chanu (@mirabai_chanu) has once again lifted India to the top of the podium. In Glasgow, she broke the Commonwealth Games record with an 85 kg snatch and a 105 kg clean and jerk, finishing with a total of 190 kg to claim her third consecutive Commonwealth gold and India’s first gold medal of 2026.
Chanu’s story began in Manipur, where carrying firewood became an unlikely training ground. That endurance took her to an Olympic silver at Tokyo 2021. It has now taken her to Glasgow, where she has further cemented her place as the face of Indian weightlifting.
The numbers speak for themselves, and so does what they represent. Women athletes in India still have to fight for the attention their achievements deserve, and every victory of Chanu’s makes that harder to ignore. With a third consecutive Commonwealth gold, she, once again, shifts the conversation around who Indian sport chooses to celebrate.
#MirabaiChanu #CWG2026

Don’t call Test Subject V (@thetestsubjectv), now streaming on JioHotstar, a transformation story. Food is simply where its central contradiction becomes impossible to ignore.
Kunal Avanti (@kunalavanti) is a chubby, middle-aged man with a back injury, an appetite for food and alcohol, and the familiar confidence of a Mumbai party boy.
Food is among the earliest forms of authority a person encounters. Parents teach us what creates strength. Culture determines what belongs on the plate. Over time, these beliefs become habits, carried forward through affection as much as instruction.
Throughout the film, Avanti pants, gasps for air, nearly gives up, and repeatedly confronts the distance between believing in compassion and reorganising a life around it.
That distance is the real subject of Test Subject V: what happens when an ordinary person realises his habits no longer reflect the person he believes himself to be?
#testsubjectV

The 2027 Pirelli Calendar brings together two systems of image-making.
Raghu Rai’s instinctive documentary practice, carried forward by Avani Rai (@avani.rai), is rooted in observation and unpredictability. Sølve Sundsbø (@solvesundsbostudio) builds images through sets, styling, and technical precision, with an eye on how they will travel across magazines, billboards, and digital platforms.
Together, they reveal how photography is changing in the age of algorithms, editing, and artificial intelligence. Sundsbø argues that every photograph manipulates through framing and styling. Rai’s approach asks what the image owes its subject, its setting, and the moment itself.
India is the frame. Photography is the real subject: what survives circulation, and what gets edited out.

posts.alt_text:
Arooj Aftab (@aroojaftab) became a symbol before many people had even heard the music. Her 2022 Grammy win for ‘Mohabbat’ made international success feel newly possible for South Asian artistes, especially women raised to believe that certain stages were simply not built with them in mind.

The milestone made Aftab a cultural shorthand for unimaginable success, as she kept moving between jazz, ghazals, Urdu poetry, and electronic riffs, refusing to turn identity into a neat creative instruction.

She understands what being first can unlock: doors that appear less firmly shut and ambitions that no longer feel faintly delusional.

Aftab’s music carries where she comes from without presenting it for inspection. Her achievement widened the scope of South Asian ambition; her career insists that representation should never become its ceiling.

Read the full interview at the link in bio.
By Arshia Dhar (@urseaa)

Milano Fashion Week is officially taking shape. Running from September 22–28, the first draft of the Spring/Summer 2027 schedule includes 60 runway shows—54 in person and six digital—alongside a season defined by major creative debuts and a growing international presence.
All eyes will be on Moschino, where new creative directors Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo will present their highly anticipated first collection for the house. The calendar also welcomes runway debuts from Marques’Almeida, Miguel Vieira, Neithan Herbert, and Victor-Hart, while three emerging labels will make their digital schedule debut.
Beyond the runways, Milan will once again blur the lines between fashion, art, and culture. Vogue World: Milan arrives on September 22 with the theme The Human Touch in the Age of Technology, celebrating Italian craftsmanship and the dialogue between tradition and innovation. The following evening, Camera Nazionale della Moda Italiana will officially open the week with a gala at Palazzo Reale, coinciding with the opening of the Dalí e la Moda exhibition.
The complete schedule—including presentations and special events—will be unveiled on September 8th.

Just this month, Chunky Panday’s (@chunkypanday) film ‘Baby Do Die Do’, an action-thriller also starring Huma Qureshi, received the sort of critical attention that has eluded him so often in his 39-year-old career. His latest role, that of a bespectacled, silver-streaked mentor to an assassin, is so far removed from Munnu, the mischievous brother in ‘Aankhen’ (1993), that you could call this a reinvention of sorts for an actor who wears the mantle of absurd comedy proudly.
The box office response to ‘Baby Do Die Do’ has kept Panday busy and filled his calendar with promotional events across India. He’s also working on a project that he signed with the late Pahlaj Nihalani, the same man who gave him his first break in movies. Then comes a Hansal Mehta production by award-winning Malayalam director Lijo Jose Pellissery, later this year.
It’s been a hectic year, but Panday is not complaining. While the intervening years since his ‘80s and ‘90s hits like ‘Tezaab’ and ‘Viswatma’ have been relatively quieter, he’s grabbing the recent spate of attention and interest with both hands. Stepping back is not an option. “Don’t let it stop. It’s the worst thing for an actor. He has to be famous till the day he dies. He can’t take it,” he says.
At the link in bio, @daribhagram chats with Panday about never slowing down, being Ananya Panday’s father, the story behind his name, and more.

posts.caption:
If you ever find yourself in the 8th arrondissement of Paris around 11 am (barring Tuesdays), you’ll notice a buzzing queue on the road flanking the Dior (@dior) flagship on Avenue Montaigne. It’s where the entrance to La Galerie—the house’s exhibition space—is located, where throngs of tourists and fashion enthusiasts line up six days a week to discover, gawk at, and take pictures of pieces from the maison’s archives in the very place they are conceived. Last month, Dior updated its permanent exhibition to include the works of Jonathan Anderson (@jonathan.anderson), the current creative director of its women’s, men’s, and haute couture collections, alongside all his predecessors, including creations by Christian Dior himself.
Spread across three floors and 13 themed rooms, the exhibition brings together about 150 garments, accessories, sketches, photographs, objects, and archival documents from the house’s history spanning almost 80 years.
At the link in bio, @chloechou13 walks us through each room of the updated Dior exhibition in Paris.
Photography: @adriendirand

posts.caption:
Gen Z called it first. The two-week annual holiday is over. You can go on micro-cations, which is truly a creative and practical way to switch off from errands, a full inbox, and all that itinerary planning. Or you could just room-rot in a destination that is equal parts scenic and comfortable. You could even draw a three-hour radius around you and end up visiting a town you may have overlooked all this while.
Project Karjat (@project_karjat), a six-villa property in Waverla village, located just two hours from Mumbai, ticks all these boxes. In fact, with all that it has to offer, it is an overachiever of sorts among the many getaways in Maharashtra that get a new lease of life come monsoon. To call Project Karjat a homestay would be underplaying the luxury it offers. To call it a resort will be ignoring its mindful design and character. A more befitting description would be your temp cosy home away from the urban rush.
At the link in bio, read @tanviii_05's full review of the property.

posts.caption:
“A year ago, if someone had told me they were pouring a kilo of salt into a baking tray before bed, I’d have assumed dinner had gone spectacularly wrong. In 2026? They’re probably salt stomping. The latest wellness ritual taking over social media is exactly what it sounds like.
If the ritual feels oddly familiar, that’s because it borrows from wellness practices already in circulation. And, like most viral wellness hacks, it doesn’t have one clear origin story. Instead, it appears to have gained traction on TikTok as a mash-up of ideas like earthing, reflexology, Epsom salt baths, and nervous system reset rituals. They’re all separate practices with varying levels of scientific evidence, but together they make salt stomping feel intuitively plausible.”
At the link in bio, @ely.nav on everything you need to know about the trending bedtime ritual.
Video courtesy: @itspaulinacee

posts.caption: Perhaps I watched too many interviews with the case because I had a hard time see the characters and not the actors. I love Matt Damon and think he is a wonderful actor but I didn’t feel much of anything for Odysseus or really any of them, apart from John Leguizamo as Eumaeus and Clytemnestra when she takes her revenge. The other thing I kept hearing about is how hard the filming 😍was and they’ve gone to all these lengths to make the film seem authentic, but for me it didn’t translate. I think it gave the actors an awesome experience, and I’m impressed later hearing about how they did some visual effects without CGI etc, but not sure how that made the movie better for me? My favorite scene was probably in Hades and Agamemnon in his armor, even though he looked too young and clean cut in it for someone who has been at war for the last 10 years. Maybe they should have done a trilogy.

posts.caption:
I genuinely LOVED sitting down and chatting with Debbie.
Fun fact, Debbie and I have been friends for over 11 years and actually found each other on Instagram when I was making my wedding dress 10 years ago. Turned out we were both working in the fashion industry (her as a garment technician, me as a textile designer) and we could gossip all day about our day to day work.
And that’s basically what we spent this episode doing!
We get into what a tech pack actually is, why a 0.3cm measurement can cause a mini crisis and the emotional cost of watching manufacturing relationships get shifted offshore chasing cheaper margins.
We also talk honestly about the parts of the industry nobody glamorises like sizing and grading gaps for larger bodies, the blame that lands on garment techs when something goes wrong in store, and why working retail first is still the best advice either of us can give anyone wanting into fashion.
It’s a conversation about the unsexy, unseen decisions that decide whether a piece of clothing actually works and why that work deserves more credit than it gets.
Listen on The Culture of Cloth podcast 🎧 link in bio

The second edition of Vogue Living has arrived just in time for long, lazy summer afternoons. In the cover story, Nataša Vojnović and her family embody the desire to step away from the chaos of everyday life and reconnect with oneself. Having traded the runways of Paris and Milan for a slower life in the picturesque surroundings of Ada Bojana, the model offers a masterclass in the art of living. In a rare interview, she opens up about family, love and why honesty is the greatest luxury of all, reminding us that summer is the ideal time to slow down, look inward and make space for what truly matters.

It's a flare-up! It's a breakout! Or is it just skin purging? While an acne breakout can emerge for any number of reasons, skin purging is what happens when a new treatment or product ramps up cell turnover and thus rapidly brings underlying blemishes to the surface of the skin. At the link in bio, we break down everything you need to know about skin purging, including how to distinguish the process from your run-of-the-mill acne breakouts.

From starring in a series of blockbusters—with an arsenal of inimitable press tour fashions in tow—to quietly marrying her longtime partner, Tom Holland, what could be next for the star? posts.alt_text:
Chaos is something @GracieAbrams has grown accustomed to. Eight years ago, she was a first-year student at Barnard with a cult fandom she’d fostered through Instagram; soon she was signed to Interscope, then on her first tour, then opening for Olivia Rodrigo and Taylor Swift. By the end of 2024, Abrams was a Grammy-nominated pop star filling arenas.

She finally took a breather last summer. “It’s not until you stop that you realize ‘Oh, I haven’t seen my friends in a long time. I haven’t cooked a meal in a long time,’” Abrams says. “The sleep schedule becomes regular for the first time in, like, four years.”

Now 26, she’s shifting into a new gear. Abrams’s third studio album, “Daughter from Hell,” out in July, sounds like her—earnest, introspective, folk-informed—but the production is more lush (“It feels like me in progress,” she says); she’s also in a happy relationship and making her first film, “Please,” with the filmmaker Halina Reijn.

For Vogue’s Summer 2026 issue, Brittany Spanos meets Gracie Abrams in Los Angeles and New York to talk about growing up, slowing down, falling in love, and where she’d like to go next. Tap the link in our bio to read the full profile. 

Photographed by @larissahofmann, Written by @brittanyspanos, Styled by @jordenbickham, Hair by @tamastuzes, Makeup by @emikaneko, Manicure by @1.800.nailme, Tailoring by Irina Tshartaryan for Susie’s Custom Designs, Produced by @hyperion.la, Set Design by  @patienceharding. Shot on location @lucasmuseum. Vogue, Summer 2026.

posts.caption:
Chaos is something @GracieAbrams has grown accustomed to. Eight years ago, she was a first-year student at Barnard with a cult fandom she’d fostered through Instagram; soon she was signed to Interscope, then on her first tour, then opening for Olivia Rodrigo and Taylor Swift. By the end of 2024, Abrams was a Grammy-nominated pop star filling arenas.
She finally took a breather last summer. “It’s not until you stop that you realize ‘Oh, I haven’t seen my friends in a long time. I haven’t cooked a meal in a long time,’” Abrams says. “The sleep schedule becomes regular for the first time in, like, four years.”
Now 26, she’s shifting into a new gear. Abrams’s third studio album, “Daughter from Hell,” out in July, sounds like her—earnest, introspective, folk-informed—but the production is more lush (“It feels like me in progress,” she says); she’s also in a happy relationship and making her first film, “Please,” with the filmmaker Halina Reijn.
For Vogue’s Summer 2026 issue, Brittany Spanos meets Gracie Abrams in Los Angeles and New York to talk about growing up, slowing down, falling in love, and where she’d like to go next. Tap the link in our bio to read the full profile.
Photographed by @larissahofmann, Written by @brittanyspanos, Styled by @jordenbickham, Hair by @tamastuzes, Makeup by @emikaneko, Manicure by @1.800.nailme, Tailoring by Irina Tshartaryan for Susie’s Custom Designs, Produced by @hyperion.la, Set Design by  @patienceharding. posts.caption:
Betye Saar, legendary Angeleno assemblage artist and central figure of the West Coast Black Arts movement, passed away at 99 on July 26. Born in Los Angeles in 1926, her mother was a seamstress, and her grandmothers painted china and made quilts—all valuable handcrafts during the Depression, when buying clothes was often out of the question. “If we wanted a new dress, we had to make it,” Saar recalls.
Saar worked as a social worker, while building a creative life through whatever means were available, and eventually joined Los Angeles’s Inner City Cultural Center as an apprentice costume designer. Over the decades that followed, Saar’s work entered the collections of institutions including the Museum of Modern Art, the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, and the Smithsonian American Art Museum. Tap the link in our bio to read more about her legacy.
Photographed by @tylersphotos

Some 35 years hence, and we’re in something of a color desert, yet some enterprising creators are looking to buck the industry trend with their whole-hearted, abundant implementation of bright, bold, brassy color. From dazzling to dreamy, punchy to poetic, meet the New Kings of Color at the link in bio.

posts.alt_text:
Chaos is something @GracieAbrams has grown accustomed to. Eight years ago, she was a first-year student at Barnard with a cult fandom she’d fostered through Instagram; soon she was signed to Interscope, then on her first tour, then opening for Olivia Rodrigo and Taylor Swift. By the end of 2024, Abrams was a Grammy-nominated pop star filling arenas.

She finally took a breather last summer. “It’s not until you stop that you realize ‘Oh, I haven’t seen my friends in a long time. I haven’t cooked a meal in a long time,’” Abrams says. “The sleep schedule becomes regular for the first time in, like, four years.”

Now 26, she’s shifting into a new gear. Abrams’s third studio album, “Daughter from Hell,” out in July, sounds like her—earnest, introspective, folk-informed—but the production is more lush (“It feels like me in progress,” she says); she’s also in a happy relationship and making her first film, “Please,” with the filmmaker Halina Reijn.

For Vogue’s Summer 2026 issue, Brittany Spanos meets Gracie Abrams in Los Angeles and New York to talk about growing up, slowing down, falling in love, and where she’d like to go next. Tap the link in our bio to read the full profile. 

Photographed by @larissahofmann, Written by @brittanyspanos, Styled by @jordenbickham, Hair by @tamastuzes, Makeup by @emikaneko, Manicure by @1.800.nailme, Tailoring by Irina Tshartaryan for Susie’s Custom Designs, Produced by @hyperion.la, Set Design by  @patienceharding. Shot on location @lucasmuseum. Vogue, Summer 2026.

posts.caption:
@aydenzs has always been in a Chinese time of his life. "Culturally speaking, I am a very, very, very Chinese person. I consume a lot of Chinese content and entertainment. Being able to act in China was a dream of mine and so it wasn’t ambition in that sense," he starts.
But it doesn't stop there. As someone who was in the Singapore National Youth Chinese Orchestra when he was younger, one of his next ventures also include a solo instrumental album that hopes to reintroduce the erhu, a Chinese two-stringed violin instrument, to modern audiences. "A lot of people think of it as a boring fuddy-duddy instrument, but I want to show that it can be interpreted for a new age."
With plenty in store, read more about our July/August cover star in the link in bio—where he shares more about whether he'll ever perform live with it, what he still dreams to do, and above all, falling in love with acting more and more.
Preorder a copy of the 'Audacity' issue fronted by Sng now in the link in bio. Out on newsstands on 11 August.

posts.alt_text:
KAVITAON KA SILSILA AA RAHA HAI @sohotheatre LONDON. 💌🫀

They say everything iconic has once happened at SOHO (@sohotheatre ). The thought that Rajkumari will now be counted among the stories told on that stage still doesn’t feel real.

It’s strange… I can often find words for emotions people have buried deep within them, but when it comes to this show~my own, I always fall short.

Rajkumari has changed my life in ways I don’t think I’ll ever fully be able to put into poetry.

The last time we were in London, we promised we’d return bigger and better.

We kept that promise.

This is our biggest London show yet, and I’d love for you to be in the room with us, to laugh, cry, heal, and become a part of this chapter.

Tickets are in my bio. See you at Soho. 🔗🤍

@tarashna.management @beacon.live

Still trying to reply to every DM, every message, every blessing… and smiling through all of them. 🥹❤️
The love you’ll have given me & Rohan has been unreal. Thank you for celebrating us like we’re your own family.
And oh my God… the love for our outfits! 🥹 Every message appreciating the tiniest personalized details, every “I noticed this,” every compliment… it truly feels like you guys see us. You saw the thought, the emotion, the intention behind every little choice we made. That means more to us than you’ll ever know. Thank you. ❤️
Everyone’s asking us the same questions—
“How did this happen?”
“How did you get married there?”
“How did you even dream of this?”
The truth is… we don’t have an answer.
Some dreams aren’t planned. They’re blessed. 🤍🕉️
If there’s one person who made all of this possible, it’s Mahadev. We were just lucky enough to be chosen.
From the bottom of our hearts… thank you for every prayer, every tear, every kind word, and every bit of love you’ve sent our way. We don’t take a single bit of it for granted.
And… ये तो सिर्फ ट्रेलर था… पिक्चर अभी बाकी है मेरे दोस्त. ❤️✨

posts.caption:
"Listen. I’m not going to be mad at anyone calling me beautiful,” @lupitanyongo says. In Director Christopher Nolan's much-anticipated, much-shrouded blockbuster adaptation of The Odyssey, Nyong'o plays Helen of Troy, the mythic face that "launched a thousand ships." When asked how it sits with her to be playing one of the most beautiful women of all time, Nyong'o responds enthusiastically, "Really well!" While many women struggle to accept a single compliment, the Oscar-winning actress is fully owning her turn as the legendary Greek figure. After all, regal, striking beauty is inextricable from Nyong'o's public identity: as Nakia, the warrior/spy and love of the late Chadwick Boseman's King T'Challa in Black Panther; as the first Black face of Lancôme; and as a Chanel ambassador. But what fans may not realize is that Nyong'o is pulling double duty in the film by portraying Helen's sister Clytemnestra too.
In our July cover story, @michandrews speaks to Nyong'o about starring in the cultural event of the summer, letting her work speak for itself, and how her ongoing battle with uterine fibroids sparked the Make Fibroids Count research campaign. Read the full interview at the link in our bio.

In our July cover story, @michandrews speaks to Nyong'o about starring in the cultural event of the summer, letting her work speak for itself, and how her ongoing battle with uterine fibroids sparked the Make Fibroids Count research campaign. Read the full interview at the link in our bio.

Inside the newly reinvented walls of @memo.paris, a new olfactory journey unfolds.
The Parisian fragrance house unveils its renewed flagship boutique at 24 rue Cambon, where space is designed as a sensory voyage.
Created with architecture studio Ciguë, the new boutique experience explores the dialogue between day and night through the changing qualities of light and natural materials. At the heart of the experience, the orientation table introduces the world of Memo Paris — the universe created by founders @iciclaramolloy and John Molloy — presenting its iconic creations and new fragrances as a map of imagined journeys. Guests are then invited into the Night Room — a unique contemplative library of scents where darkness heightens the senses. Designed to create a deeper connection with fragrance, this intimate setting invites visitors to slow down and explore a fully personalized experience.
Explore the new Memo Paris boutique at 24 rue Cambon in Paris, a new space dedicated to the art of fragrance.
